question: What are the three main pillars of health care financing?

options.A: Revenue collection, risk pooling, and purchasing

explanation: Health care financing relies on collecting revenue, pooling risks together, and purchasing services for the population. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is risk pooling considered a core function of health financing?

options.A: It shares the financial burden of illness across a larger group of people
options.B: It ensures that hospitals receive immediate cash payments for services
options.C: It eliminates the need for private health insurance companies entirely
options.D: It allows the government to collect higher taxes from wealthy citizens

explanation: Risk pooling protects individuals from catastrophic health costs by spreading the financial risk of sickness across a healthy and sick population. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which financing mechanism requires patients to pay cash directly at the point of service?
explanation: Out-of-pocket spending refers to direct cash payments made by patients to healthcare providers at the time they receive care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h2)

question: Out-of-pocket payments are described as regressive because they do what?

options.A: Impose a heavier financial burden on poor households than on rich ones
options.B: Reduce the total amount of money collected by the federal government
options.C: Provide free medical care exclusively to high-income earners
options.D: Increase the administrative costs of running public hospitals

explanation: Regressive financing takes a larger percentage of income from low-income earners, making healthcare unaffordable for the poor. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of risk pooling in a health system?

options.A: To generate profits for private insurance companies
options.B: To spread the financial risk of illness across a large population
options.C: To reduce the number of patients visiting tertiary hospitals
options.D: To increase the salaries of healthcare workers in rural areas

explanation: Risk pooling gathers funds so that the rare, heavy cost of severe illness is shared by many rather than borne by the sick person alone. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h3)

question: How does strategic purchasing differ from traditional passive budgeting?

options.A: It prevents patients from choosing their preferred healthcare providers
options.B: It eliminates the need for any administrative oversight of hospitals
options.C: It relies entirely on out-of-pocket donations from international agencies
options.D: It actively ties provider payments to service quality and performance

explanation: Strategic purchasing involves actively deciding which services to buy, from whom, and how to pay to maximize health outcomes. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary regulatory body for health insurance in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The National Health Insurance Authority regulates, promotes, and integrates health insurance schemes throughout Nigeria. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h4)

question: State Health Insurance Schemes are primarily designed to target which group of people?

options.A: Workers in the informal sector and rural populations
options.B: Expatriates working in multinational oil companies
options.C: Federal civil servants with mandatory formal deductions
options.D: High-income earners seeking specialized foreign care

explanation: State schemes bridge the coverage gap by bringing informal sector workers and rural communities into subsidized insurance pools. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which financing challenge is directly linked to the Abuja Declaration target?

options.A: High cost of imported medical diagnostic equipment
options.B: Rapid migration of nurses to foreign countries
options.C: Excessive reliance on private health maintenance organizations

explanation: The Abuja Declaration urged African governments to allocate at least 15% of their annual budget to the health sector, a target many still miss. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why does a large informal economy make health insurance coverage difficult to achieve?

options.A: Workers lack fixed monthly salaries, making regular premium collection hard
options.B: Private insurance companies refuse to register any business in rural areas
options.C: The government automatically provides free care to all informal traders
options.D: Informal workers are legally exempted from participating in national schemes

explanation: Without steady payroll deductions, collecting voluntary contributions from daily wage earners requires intensive community outreach and flexible payment models. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the ultimate goal of Universal Health Coverage?

options.A: Total privatization of hospitals to increase service speed
options.B: Access to needed health services without financial hardship
options.C: Eradication of all chronic infectious diseases by a set year
options.D: Free treatment for all citizens in foreign medical facilities

explanation: UHC guarantees that everyone can access preventive, curative, and rehabilitative health services without facing financial ruin. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why is strengthening Primary Health Care essential for achieving sustainable health financing?

options.A: It generates massive profits that can fund tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: It ensures that patients bypass local clinics and go straight to specialists
options.C: It prevents costly conditions by managing health issues early at the community level
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses and doctors in rural health posts

explanation: Investing in primary care is cost-effective because it resolves health problems before they require expensive hospitalization or complex tertiary interventions. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h6)

question: How do clinical nurses directly influence health care resource allocation on the ward?

options.A: By preventing waste of medical consumables and reducing extended hospital stays
options.B: By setting the official pricing tariffs for drugs purchased by the hospital
options.C: By negotiating insurance premium rates directly with corporate employers
options.D: By collecting annual taxes from the surrounding local community

explanation: Nurses manage daily ward supplies and prevent complications like infections, directly controlling the cost of patient care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h7)

question: A nurse who advocates for an indigent patient to access hospital welfare funds is participating in what aspect of care?

options.A: Enforcing mandatory health insurance tax deductions
options.B: Performing strategic health sector economic forecasting
options.C: Mitigating financial barriers to healthcare access

explanation: Connecting vulnerable patients to financial aid helps bridge the gap between high out-of-pocket costs and necessary clinical care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h7)
